title: Review of c01's phase_membrane BD twin: replicated on fresh seeds 9 and 10; the uniform-D twin keeps division but loses the L ring (1.13-1.17 at lam 0.1, 1.43 at lam 0.01, vs 2.29-2.39)
summary: Looked at L_compare.png and the twin sheets, then ran phase_membrane and the finding's twin_pm.py (gate=0, chi=0, lam=0.1) on fresh seed 9 with labkit (T=8000) and the finding's ringmeasure.py on seeds 9 and 10, plus lam=0.01 on seed 9. Per-cell L ring (rim / deep core, median over cells at t=8000): phase_membrane 2.39 and 2.29 (rim/outside 18.5, 8.3); twin lam 0.1: 1.13 and 1.17; twin lam 0.01: 1.43. The twin still forms walled cells from noise and divides (rerun_twin/seed9: 24 persistent splits, generation 3, against 9 and generation 3 for phase_membrane), with smaller, more uniform cells (inradius 3.6-4 vs 7-7.4 px). The finding's reading holds: B, not D, needs the gated mobility and wall drift.

observations.B: ring/summary.txt: ring 2.39/2.29 (world, seeds 9/10) vs 1.13/1.17 (twin lam 0.1) and 1.43 (lam 0.01); rerun_pm/seed9/sheet.png vs rerun_twin/seed9/sheet.png t=4000-8000

controls_run.B: rerun_twin/ and ring/ring_twin_*.json: the finding's matched uniform-D twin on fresh seeds

not_checked: lam 0.001 lattice-locked case and its 2x run
verdicts.limitation: I checked only lam 0.1 and 0.01; the claim that the only ring-keeping twin (lam 0.001) fails at 2x rests on the author's single run. The ring measure uses a size-normalized core, and twin cells are about half the size, which may lower the ring a little by itself.
